newsitem.title: philippines: Philippine peso slightly down on arbitrage play.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso slightly down on arbitrage play.

text.p: * Turnover swells to $212.50 million from $135.38 million
The Philippine peso ended a tad lower in active trades on Thursday at 26.285 from 26.284 on arbitrage play for the long weekend, traders said.
But the day's average yielded a stronger peso at 26.282 to the dollar from 26.285 as the Central Bank became a net seller of dollars at 26.285.
Banks were selling their dollars for same-day delivery so they could have more pesos during the long weekend, dealers said.
The peso is more attractive to hold because of its higher interest premium over the dollar, dealers said.
At the same time, banks were buying back dollars they sold for delivery on Monday.
One dealer said some banks attempted to buy up the dollar so they could book month-end revaluation gains.
"The Central Bank, however, made it clear it didn't want the dollar to go beyond the 26.285 level," he said.
On Monday, in the absence of any developments, the peso will just follow where the Central Bank wants it to be, traders said.
